stages.label: The wilderness (Exodus route)

quotes.quote: they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water.

stages.text: The wilderness: a vast arid tableland of pale sand, gravel plains and dark rock outcrops rising to bare mountains, scattered with thorn scrub and sparse grasses in the wadis. canon.note: Younger twin son of Isaac and Rebekah, renamed Israel after wrestling with God and father of the twelve sons; the central patriarch of Genesis, also referenced by name in Hosea, Obadiah, Malachi and the New Testament letters.

stages.label: Jacob

stages.text: Jacob: a slender, wiry man of middle to later years in his prime and sixties-to-seventies in old age; lean, sinewy build from long herding; smooth, unhairy skin browned by sun; dark, close-cropped hair and short beard kept trim; alert, thoughtful eyes and a clean, quiet face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic and wool wrap cloak in earth brown, with leather sandals. Carries a shepherd's staff.

canon.name: Esau

stages.label: Esau

stages.text: Esau: man of about forty to sixty, broad-shouldered and weathered from the field; ruddy, sun-darkened skin; thick dark-red hair and a full reddish beard; hairy forearms and hands; heavy brow and steady dark eyes. fields.timeOfDay: Late afternoon sliding toward dusk, clear dry sky with a light wind.

canon.name: Moses
canon.note: Israel's lawgiver and leader who led the people out of Egypt, received the law at Sinai and is named across the Old and New Testament divisions as the same individual, distinguished only by the sections in which he appears or is mentioned.

stages.label: Moses, elder

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

stages.text: Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.

stages.label: Moses, infant

quotes.quote: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

stages.text: Moses: a newborn infant; soft smooth skin; a small round face; a little dark hair; wrapped in plain linen cloth and laid in a woven reed basket sealed with bitumen and pitch; no beard, no staff, no adult clothing.

stages.label: Moses, adult

quotes.quote: But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

stages.text: Moses: a man of about forty; lean, strong, well-proportioned build; brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard; alert, sober face; a knee-length undyed linen tunic with a dark woven wool cloak of brown and grey pinned at the shoulder; he carries a plain wooden shepherd's staff.

quotes.quote: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt
You shall tell the children of Israel this

Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.

stages.label: The plains of Moab

canon.name: David son of Jesse (king of Israel)

stages.label: David as king

quotes.quote: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.

stages.text: David: a man of about thirty to fifty, athletic and broad-shouldered, of medium height; ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes, short dark beard trimmed close; dark hair cut to the shoulder. Signature outfit: a long blue royal robe with a sash of crimson and gold, over an undertunic of white linen. Carries a bronze-bossed sword in a leather scabbard and a harp.

stages.label: David as youth

quotes.quote: He sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with a handsome face and good appearance. Yahweh said, “Arise! Anoint him, for this is he.”

stages.text: David: a beardless youth and young adult before kingship; slender, wiry build, ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes and short dark curly hair. Plain undyed brown wool tunic, leather belt and sandals; shepherd's pouch and sling when called for. No crown or royal robes.

stages.label: David as elder

quotes.quote: Now King David was old and advanced in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he couldn’t keep warm.

stages.text: David: an old man of about seventy, lean and bent with age, his frame still dignified; ruddy complexion faded to a weathered warmth, dark eyes deep-set and gentle, white hair and a white beard cut short. Signature outfit: a plain long wool robe of undyed cream with a dark blue cloak over the shoulders for warmth. Carries a staff of almond wood.

canon.name: Hiram of Tyre
canon.note: King of Tyre who sends cedar to David's house.

stages.label: Hiram of Tyre

quotes.quote: Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon
I will do all your desire concerning timber of cedar, and concerning cypress timber.

stages.text: Hiram of Tyre: man of middle to advanced age, late forties to sixties; sturdy build; olive-bronze skin; dark hair and short trimmed beard streaked with grey; dignified, weathered face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long purple-dyed wool robe with a woven gold-threaded border over a white linen tunic, and a gold-banded headdress. Signature prop: a gold signet ring on his right hand.

canon.name: Valley of Rephaim
canon.note: Valley where the Philistines raid and David inquires of God.

stages.label: Valley of Rephaim

quotes.quote: the army of the Philistines were encamped in the valley of Rephaim

stages.text: Valley of Rephaim: a broad, shallow valley of pale limestone soil running between rounded Judean hills south-west of Jerusalem; terraced olive groves and scattered terebinth trees on the slopes, dry grass and stony ground on the valley floor; low stone field walls, a few watchtowers of rough-hewn stone on the ridges, and a dry watercourse winding through the middle.

fields.primarySubject: Heap of carved idols on the ground, flames rising from them, Israelite soldiers near.

fields.setting: Open terrain in the Valley of Rephaim, scattered stone and olive scrub, Jerusalem's walls visible on the rise.
fields.secondaryElements: Soldiers in tunics and armor tending the pyre, David in royal robes at a distance, smoke drifting across the valley.
fields.mood: Solemn, triumphant and austere, with weight rather than celebration.
fields.timeOfDay: Late afternoon turning to dusk, clear dry air with light haze of smoke.
fields.composition: Wide view from a slight rise, the fire and idol heap in the foreground, David and soldiers in the middle ground, city walls on the horizon.

previous.text: They are all hot as an oven, and devour their judges. All their kings have fallen. There is no one among them who calls to me.

next.text: Strangers have devoured his strength, and he doesn’t realize it. Indeed, gray hairs are here and there on him, and he doesn’t realize it.

section.title: Corruption of the court and alliances

aliases: those who came out of Egypt
canon.name: The Israelite people (the children of Israel)
canon.note: The collective Israelite nation across Exodus through Malachi and Hebrews, one body whose different portrayals (marching nation, assembly, covenant people, judged northern kingdom, returned community, wilderness generation) are all the same people; distinguish only from the returned community of Nehemiah in the note by the Judah/Jerusalem setting, but these are the same people.

stages.label: The Israelite people

quotes.quote: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt
You shall tell the children of Israel this
So they shall put my name on the children of Israel; and I will bless them.

stages.text: The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.

aliases: the God of our Lord Jesus Christ
him who sits on the throne
canon.name: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel
canon.note: The one God, creator and speaker of the Old Testament and the Father of Jesus Christ in the New Testament; distinct from Jesus in every entry.

stages.label: God the Father (radiance and cloud)

quotes.quote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.

stages.text: God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

canon.name: Israel (Hosea)
canon.note: The northern kingdom, the setting of Hosea's oracles and the land of Israel.

stages.label: Israel (the northern kingdom)

quotes.quote: Israel is a luxuriant vine that produces his fruit.
I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness.
The high places also of Aven, the sin of Israel, will be destroyed.
Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces

stages.text: Israel: the northern kingdom in the hill country of Ephraim, terraced hillsides and rolling highlands under a wide sky. Vineyards climb the slopes, fig trees stand near threshing floors, and grain fields spread across the valley of Jezreel. Walled cities of fortified stone crown the hills, with royal palaces of cedar and dressed stone and sanctuaries with high places, altars and standing sacred stones at Bethel and Gilgal. Thorn and thistle grow on the ruined altars, and the distant mountains of Tabor and Gilboa rise beyond.

fields.primarySubject: Ephraim, the northern kingdom's figure, standing mid-gesture among the foreign envoys, half-turned and unbalanced
fields.action: Ephraim is caught mingling with foreign envoys at the palace gate, drawn into their company and alliances
fields.setting: A walled Israelite city's court gate, with a palace courtyard behind and dusty road beyond
fields.secondaryElements: Foreign envoys in Assyrian-style garments and bronze armor; Israelite officials in dyed court robes; a half-cooked round flatbread on a clay griddle nearby; wayside shrine smoke
fields.mood: Uneasy, tense and quietly sorrowful, with a sense of drift and compromise
fields.timeOfDay: Late afternoon sliding toward dusk, warm gold light turning dim amber
fields.composition: Medium-wide view from the gate, Ephraim at center-left among the envoys, the courtyard opening behind, the sky and diffuse radiance spread across the upper frame

moment.text: So Jeremiah stayed in the court of the guard until the day that Jerusalem was taken.

previous.text: Then all the princes came to Jeremiah, and asked him; and he told them according to all these words that the king had commanded. So they stopped speaking with him, for the matter was not perceived.

section.title: Jeremiah in the cistern

canon.name: Jeremiah son of Hilkiah
canon.note: Prophet from Anathoth who speaks most of the book.

stages.label: Jeremiah

quotes.quote: The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, one of the priests who were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
They let down Jeremiah with cords. In the dungeon there was no water, but mire; and Jeremiah sank in the mire.

stages.text: Jeremiah: a man in his middle years, lean and weathered from long journeys and imprisonment, with a grave, careworn face and deep-set dark eyes. Close-cropped dark hair and a short greying beard. Dark-skinned Levantine complexion. Wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic under a long brown wool cloak, the cloak worn thin at the hem. Carries a plain wooden staff.

canon.name: Zedekiah
canon.note: Judean king set up by Babylon, also called Mattaniah, who rebels and is exiled.

stages.label: Zedekiah, king of Judah

quotes.quote: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign. He reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
He put out the eyes of Zedekiah; and the king of Babylon bound him in fetters, and carried him to Babylon

stages.text: Zedekiah: a man in his early thirties, of middle height and sturdy build, with olive-brown skin, close-cropped dark hair and a short trimmed beard. Lined brow, watchful dark eyes, a strong nose and a face worn by grief and strain. Signature outfit: a long blue-violet royal court robe over a linen tunic, with a fringed woollen cloak in deep red-brown. Carries a plain gold-banded royal staff.

canon.name: Ebedmelech
canon.note: The Ethiopian eunuch in King Zedekiah's court in Jeremiah who pleads for the prophet and rescues him from the cistern; served the king of Judah, not the queen of Ethiopia.

stages.label: Ebedmelech the Ethiopian

quotes.quote: Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, a eunuch, who was in the king’s house
took from there rags and worn-out garments

stages.text: Ebedmelech: a man of middle years, lean and upright, with dark brown skin and close-cropped black hair. He is beardless, as a court eunuch, with a calm, steady face. He wears a plain undyed linen tunic to the knee under a long cloak of dark blue wool, belted with cord. He carries a rolled cloth of rags and worn garments over one arm.

canon.name: Pashhur son of Malchijah
canon.note: Official sent by Zedekiah to consult Jeremiah (ch. 21) and later a prince who casts Jeremiah into the dungeon (ch. 38). Distinct from Pashhur son of Immer.

stages.label: Pashhur son of Malchijah

quotes.quote: King Zedekiah sent to him Pashhur the son of Malchijah
Pashhur the son of Malchijah heard the words that Jeremiah spoke

stages.text: Pashhur son of Malchijah: a man of about fifty, of middle height and sturdy build; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard streaked with grey; lined brow and steady, careful eyes. Signature outfit: a long court robe of deep blue wool with a woven band of ochre at the hem and cuffs, over a white linen tunic, and a belt of bronze plates. Carries a seal ring of dark stone on a cord.

canon.name: The court of the guard
canon.note: The prison court in Jerusalem where Jeremiah is confined under Zedekiah (also the cistern dungeon of Malchijah, the same confinement); distinct from the Egyptian prison and from the wilderness/exile setting.

stages.label: The court of the guard

quotes.quote: Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the guard, which was in the king of Judah’s house.
In the dungeon there was no water, but mire; and Jeremiah sank in the mire.

stages.text: The court of the guard: an enclosed courtyard within the king's house in Jerusalem, paved with worn limestone flags and walled by rough-hewn stone and mud brick. A low gate of cedar and iron opens onto the palace precincts. A stone-lined cistern pit in one corner, its rim worn smooth by cords, holds dark mire. Sparse dry grass and a single fig tree grow in cracks.

aliases: the city of my fathers' tombs
canon.name: Jerusalem
canon.note: The capital city of Judah (also called Jebus, David's city, the holy city, Zion as city in some books); the city itself, distinct from the hill/mountain of Zion as a place of Yahweh's dwelling.

stages.label: Jerusalem

quotes.quote: they buried him in David's city
a breach was made in the city

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs crowd the slopes; a fortified citadel of the stronghold of Zion stands on the high ground. Massive city walls with gates, and above the city the temple mount crowned by a stone-built temple of Yahweh.

fields.primarySubject: Jeremiah seated quietly on the ground in the guard court, head bowed, worn cloak drawn around him.
fields.action: He waits in stillness while distant smoke rises over the city walls.
fields.setting: A walled court inside the palace compound of Jerusalem, with stone pavement and a guard post.
fields.secondaryElements: Armed guards with spears stand near the gate; a faint plume of smoke and dust rises above the distant walls.
fields.mood: Solemn, grieving and resigned, with quiet dignity.
fields.timeOfDay: Late afternoon in dry, dusty siege heat, hazy sky, light fading toward evening.
fields.composition: Wide view from low across the court, Jeremiah small in the lower centre, guards and walls framing the edges, smoke rising in the upper distance.

moment.text: Her nobles were purer than snow. They were whiter than milk. They were more ruddy in body than rubies. Their polishing was like sapphire.

previous.text: For the iniquity of the daughter of my people is greater than the sin of Sodom, which was overthrown as in a moment. No hands were laid on her.

next.text: Their appearance is blacker than a coal. They are not known in the streets. Their skin clings to their bones. It is withered. It has become like wood.

section.title: The city's ruin, the priests' guilt and Edom's doom

canon.name: Zion
canon.note: Personified city of Jerusalem as a mourning widow and captive princess, speaking in the first person in Lamentations 1 and 2; distinct from the collective people of Judah and Jerusalem.

stages.label: Zion, the mourning city-woman

quotes.quote: She has become as a widow, who was great among the nations!
All her gates are desolate. Her priests sigh.
They have clothed themselves with sackcloth. The virgins of Jerusalem hang down their heads to the ground.

stages.text: Zion: a woman of middle years, dignified and grieving, with dark hair bound low and partly veiled, olive skin darkened by ash and dust. Her features are worn and sorrowful. She wears a plain undyed linen robe under a dark sackcloth mantle of brown and grey, with a torn hem. She carries no regalia.

canon.name: Children of Zion (Lamentations)
canon.note: Infants and children who faint in the streets or beg for bread in Lamentations.

stages.label: Children of Zion

quotes.quote: the young children and the infants swoon in the streets of the city
The precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold
The tongue of the nursing child clings to the roof of his mouth for thirst.

stages.text: Children of Zion: young boys and girls aged about four to twelve, with slight thin builds worn down by hunger; olive to brown skin dulled with dust; dark hair cropped short or tied back; large dark eyes and sunken cheeks. Plain undyed linen or wool tunics belted with cord, faded to grey-brown, bare feet dusty. Signature prop: a small clay jar or pitcher held close.

canon.name: The priests of Jerusalem
canon.note: Collective body of priests in Lamentations who are killed in the sanctuary; a group, not an individual.

stages.label: Priests of Jerusalem

quotes.quote: Her priests sigh.
Should the priest and the prophet be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?

stages.text: The priests of Jerusalem: men of middle to later years, lean and dignified, with dark-brown skin, short dark hair and a neatly kept beard flecked with grey. Calm, grave faces marked by sorrow. Signature outfit: a white linen priestly tunic and a linen headband, with a blue-violet cloak over the shoulders. Carry only a bronze censer.

canon.name: Prophets of Jerusalem
canon.note: The prophets of Jerusalem who gave false visions and are blamed for the city's fall, as portrayed in Lamentations.

stages.label: Prophets of Jerusalem

quotes.quote: her prophets find no vision from Yahweh
the sins of her prophets and the iniquities of her priests

stages.text: Prophets of Jerusalem: men in middle age, lean and weathered, with dark skin tanned by sun and a sturdy build. Short dark beards, hair cropped at the neck, deep-set attentive eyes. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a dull ochre wool cloak. Each carries a plain wooden staff.

canon.name: The enemies (Jerusalem's foreign adversaries)
canon.note: Collective invaders and persecutors who destroy Jerusalem in Lamentations; a human/national group, not the divine accuser, so keep separate from Satan.

stages.label: The enemies (Jerusalem's foreign adversaries)

quotes.quote: Her adversaries have become the head. Her enemies prosper

stages.text: The enemies: adult men of the Mesopotamian and neighbouring Levantine peoples, aged twenty to fifty, lean and hardened by campaign. Skin weathered tan to olive-brown. Hair short or bound back, beards trimmed close. Stern, watchful faces. Typical dress: a sleeveless or short-sleeved tunic of undyed wool with a leather belt, a bronze-scaled or leather armour, and a dusty brown cloak. Colours: ochre, rust and iron-grey. Carries a spear or curved sword; no other props.

him who sits on the throne

canon.note: The one God, creator and speaker of the Old Testament and the Father of Jesus Christ in the New Testament; distinct from Jesus in every entry.

quotes.quote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.

canon.note: The capital city of Judah (also called Jebus, David's city, the holy city, Zion as city in some books); the city itself, distinct from the hill/mountain of Zion as a place of Yahweh's dwelling.

stages.label: Jerusalem

quotes.quote: they buried him in David's city
a breach was made in the city

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs crowd the slopes; a fortified citadel of the stronghold of Zion stands on the high ground. Massive city walls with gates, and above the city the temple mount crowned by a stone-built temple of Yahweh.

canon.name: The streets of the city
canon.note: Streets and roads where the children faint, the dead lie and the blind wander.

stages.label: The streets of the city

quotes.quote: The roads to Zion mourn, because no one comes to the solemn assembly.
All her gates are desolate.
The stones of the sanctuary are poured out at the head of every street.

stages.text: The streets of the city: narrow, unpaved or rough-stoned lanes winding between low flat-roofed houses of mud brick and dressed limestone, with broken walls and ruined doorways. Dust and ash lie thick; some stones of the sanctuary and fallen gold-toned debris lie at the corners. Sparse dry scrub grows in cracks, and gates stand desolate at the end of roads leading up toward Zion.

aliases: the house which is called by my name
the tent of the daughter of Zion
the house of Yahweh of Armies
canon.name: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem (the temple)
canon.note: The one Jerusalem temple (Yahweh's house, the sanctuary on Mount Moriah) across all references, from Solomon's building through repair, destruction and rebuilding; construction and ruin are later appearance stages, not separate places.

stages.label: Solomon's temple on Mount Moriah

quotes.quote: The house, when it was under construction, was built of stone prepared at the quarry
Within the inner sanctuary was twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in width, and twenty cubits in its height.
He overlaid the floor of the house with gold, inside and outside.
Also he made before the house two pillars thirty-five cubits high
He set the sea on the right side of the house eastward and toward the south.

stages.text: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem: a stone temple of finished ashlar on Mount Moriah, roofed with cedar beams, its inner sanctuary panelled in cedar and overlaid with pure gold. Carved cherubim, palm and open flowers cover the doors and walls. Before the house stand two great bronze pillars and a huge bronze molten sea on twelve oxen. Courts of stone surround it, with olive and cypress trees, and the walled city of Jerusalem rises beyond.

aliases: Edom in the land of Uz
canon.name: The wilderness and exile
canon.note: The Lamentations setting of captivity, pursuit and hiding where the exiles dwell or are hunted; a different place from the Egyptian prison despite the shared alias 'the dungeon'.

stages.label: The wilderness and exile

quotes.quote: She dwells among the nations. She finds no rest.
They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and have cast a stone on me.
The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of Yahweh, was taken in their pits

stages.text: The wilderness and exile: arid highland and dry steppe under a pale sky, scattered with stony ravines, cisterns cut into rock, and low flat-roofed mud-brick dwellings and walled settlements of foreign towns. Sparse thorn scrub and dry grass, a few gnarled terebinths, and distant ruined walls of a broken city on the horizon.

fields.primarySubject: A group of noble figures standing upright, their pale garments shining white and their faces calm and dignified.
fields.action: They stand still in the ruined street, appearing untouched and radiant amid the destruction around them.
fields.setting: A broken street in the ruined city of Jerusalem, with fallen stones and dust underfoot.
fields.secondaryElements: Faint glowing embers and drifting smoke in the background, with ruined walls and gates behind them.
fields.mood: Sorrowful, reverent and haunted, with a sense of lost dignity and beauty.
fields.timeOfDay: Dusk fading toward dawn, with dim ash-coloured light and a faint glow from distant fire.
fields.composition: Viewed slightly from below at mid-distance, the nobles arranged in a loose group across the middle of the frame with ruins framing them.

moment.text: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David’s sons were chief ministers.

previous.text: Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar were priests, Seraiah was scribe,

section.title: David's officials

aliases: the anointed of the God of Jacob
canon.name: David son of Jesse (king of Israel)
canon.note: The single David of the Hebrew books and the New Testament references: son of Jesse, shepherd, harpist, anointed king, father of Solomon; all entries describe this one king and the hint's second David is not needed.

stages.label: David as king

quotes.quote: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.

stages.text: David: a man of about thirty to fifty, athletic and broad-shouldered, of medium height; ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes, short dark beard trimmed close; dark hair cut to the shoulder. Signature outfit: a long blue royal robe with a sash of crimson and gold, over an undertunic of white linen. Carries a bronze-bossed sword in a leather scabbard and a harp.

stages.label: David as youth

quotes.quote: He sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with a handsome face and good appearance. Yahweh said, “Arise! Anoint him, for this is he.”

stages.text: David: a beardless youth and young adult before kingship; slender, wiry build, ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes and short dark curly hair. Plain undyed brown wool tunic, leather belt and sandals; shepherd's pouch and sling when called for. No crown or royal robes.

stages.label: David as elder

quotes.quote: Now King David was old and advanced in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he couldn’t keep warm.

stages.text: David: an old man of about seventy, lean and bent with age, his frame still dignified; ruddy complexion faded to a weathered warmth, dark eyes deep-set and gentle, white hair and a white beard cut short. Signature outfit: a plain long wool robe of undyed cream with a dark blue cloak over the shoulders for warmth. Carries a staff of almond wood.

canon.name: Joab
canon.note: Son of Zeruiah and David's army commander, who kills Abner, Absalom and Amasa and leads the Ammonite campaign; distinguish from other Joabs by his role as David's commander in the army.

stages.label: Joab, captain of David's army

quotes.quote: Joab was clothed in his apparel of war that he had put on, and on it was a sash with a sword fastened on his waist in its sheath
He took three darts in his hand and thrust them through Absalom’s heart
Ten young men who bore Joab’s armor surrounded and struck Absalom

stages.text: Joab: a man in his middle years, around forty to fifty, of strong, weathered build with broad shoulders and a soldier's stance. Skin olive-brown and sun-browned. Dark hair cropped short at the neck, with a close-trimmed beard streaked with grey at the chin. Hard, watchful face with a broken nose. Signature outfit: a bronze-scaled or leather-plated military coat over a dark undertunic, with a deep red-brown war sash at the waist. Carries a sword in a plain sheath and three darts in hand.

aliases: the city of my fathers' tombs
canon.name: Jerusalem
canon.note: The capital city of Judah (also called Jebus, David's city, the holy city, Zion as city in some books); the city itself, distinct from the hill/mountain of Zion as a place of Yahweh's dwelling.

stages.label: Jerusalem

quotes.quote: they buried him in David's city
a breach was made in the city

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs crowd the slopes; a fortified citadel of the stronghold of Zion stands on the high ground. Massive city walls with gates, and above the city the temple mount crowned by a stone-built temple of Yahweh.

fields.primarySubject: Benaiah son of Jehoiada standing at the head of the royal guard, cloaked and armed
fields.action: Benaiah receiving and holding his post over the royal bodyguard, guardsmen standing ready in formation
fields.setting: Stone courtyard of the royal palace in Jerusalem with gates and walls
fields.secondaryElements: Armed Cherethite and Pelethite guardsmen in period armor, a few court attendants at the palace doors
fields.mood: Ordered, dignified and steady, with quiet loyalty
fields.timeOfDay: Late morning, clear dry warm sky with light cloud
fields.composition: Benaiah centered in mid-ground, guards arranged in ranks on either side, palace walls framing the view

moment.text: Jacob said to Pharaoh, “The years of my pilgrimage are one hundred thirty years. The days of the years of my life have been few and evil. They have not attained to the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage.”

previous.text: Pharaoh said to Jacob, “How old are you?”

next.text: Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from the presence of Pharaoh.

section.title: Jacob presented to Pharaoh

canon.name: Joseph son of Jacob (the dreamer)
canon.note: Favorite son of Jacob and Rachel, sold into Egypt and later ruler under Pharaoh; the Genesis figure, also named in Judges as the house of Joseph's ancestor, Acts and Hebrews as the patriarch; not the husband of Mary.

stages.label: Joseph, son of Jacob

quotes.quote: Joseph, being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brothers.
Joseph was well-built and handsome.
he made him a tunic of many colors.
arrayed him in robes of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck.
Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt.
Joseph lived one hundred ten years.

stages.text: Joseph: a young man of about seventeen in youth, rising to a mature man of thirty and later an elder of one hundred ten; well-built and handsome, lean and strong from shepherding, with warm brown skin, dark hair cut short, a smooth-shaven face in Egyptian style, dark eyes and a steady, gentle expression. Signature outfit: a long tunic of many colours in Canaanite style, bright reds, blues and yellows; in Egypt, robes of white or cream fine linen. Signature props: a gold chain at the neck and Pharaoh's signet ring on the hand.

canon.name: Jacob
canon.note: Younger twin son of Isaac and Rebekah, renamed Israel after wrestling with God and father of the twelve sons; the central patriarch of Genesis, also referenced by name in Hosea, Obadiah, Malachi and the New Testament letters.

stages.label: Jacob

quotes.quote: The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.
Isn’t he rightly named Jacob?
his hand had hold on Esau’s heel
leaning on the top of his staff.

stages.text: Jacob: a slender, wiry man of middle to later years in his prime and sixties-to-seventies in old age; lean, sinewy build from long herding; smooth, unhairy skin browned by sun; dark, close-cropped hair and short beard kept trim; alert, thoughtful eyes and a clean, quiet face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic and wool wrap cloak in earth brown, with leather sandals. Carries a shepherd's staff.

canon.name: Pharaoh of Joseph
canon.note: Egyptian king of Joseph's era who dreams of cattle and grain and elevates Joseph; the king who knew Joseph, distinct from the Exodus oppressor.

stages.label: Pharaoh of Joseph

quotes.quote: Pharaoh took off his signet ring from his hand, and put it on Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in robes of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck.

stages.text: Pharaoh of Joseph: man in his fifties; broad, dignified build; deep bronze skin; close-cropped dark hair under a tall blue and gold royal headcloth with a cobra emblem; neatly trimmed beard, ceremonial false beard; calm, grave face. Signature outfit: white pleated linen kilt and shendyt with a broad golden collar in blue and gold. Props: gold signet ring, gold chain, crook and flail of office.

canon.name: Joseph's brothers
canon.note: The ten sons of Jacob who sell Joseph and later go to Egypt for grain; the Genesis band of brothers, distinct from the brothers of Jesus.

stages.label: Joseph's brothers

quotes.quote: The sons of Israel came to buy among those who came, for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
the sons of Israel carried Jacob, their father, their little ones, and their wives, in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent

stages.text: Joseph's brothers: men aged roughly twenty to fifty, sturdy herders of lean, weathered build; olive-brown skin tanned by sun and wind; short dark hair and close-trimmed beards streaked with dust; lined faces, steady and careworn. Signature outfit: a plain undyed wool tunic of ochre-brown with a darker woollen wrap and leather sandals. Signature prop: a shepherd's crook carried by one brother alone.

canon.name: Pharaoh's house
canon.note: Royal residence and court of Pharaoh in Genesis where dreams are told and Joseph is brought before the king; distinct from the other courts in this group.

stages.label: Pharaoh's house
stages.text: Pharaoh's house: royal palace of mud-brick and limestone on a raised terrace above the Nile floodplain; tall painted pylon gateway, columned hall with papyrus-bud capitals, shaded courtyards, cool stone floors; date palms, sycamores and green reeds along the river edge; the great river and irrigated fields visible beyond the walls.

canon.name: Goshen
canon.note: Fertile Egyptian region where Jacob's family settles and where Israel is spared plagues in Exodus; same region in both books.

stages.label: Goshen

quotes.quote: they came into the land of Goshen
they got themselves possessions therein, and were fruitful, and multiplied exceedingly
Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, there was no hail.

stages.text: Goshen: green pastoral delta land in eastern Egypt, lush grass and fields watered by canals from the Nile, reed-edged channels, scattered acacia and sycamore, date palms by the waterways. Settlement of mud-brick and reed-and-wattle houses and pens among tents of goats' hair, sheepfolds of stone and brush, and grain storehouses; a fortified Egyptian town wall visible at the distance.

fields.primarySubject: Jacob, an elderly herder with a worn staff, standing before the throne with head slightly bowed.
fields.action: Jacob gives his weary answer about the years of his pilgrimage, as Pharaoh listens from his seat.
fields.setting: Royal audience hall of mud-brick and stone with a raised dais, and green Goshen pastures visible beyond the palace.
fields.secondaryElements: Pharaoh seated on a simple throne in fine linen; a few unnamed court attendants stand at the edges of the hall.
fields.mood: Reflective, weary and dignified, with quiet grief.
fields.timeOfDay: Late afternoon, clear and dry, warm golden light slanting through high windows.
fields.composition: Medium shot from the side of the hall, Jacob in the foreground at left facing the seated Pharaoh at right, the green pastures faintly beyond.

Close-cropped dark hair and a short greying beard. Dark-skinned Levantine complexion. Wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic under a long brown wool cloak, the cloak worn thin at the hem. Carries a plain wooden staff.

aliases: the city of my fathers' tombs
canon.name: Jerusalem
canon.note: The capital city of Judah (also called Jebus, David's city, the holy city, Zion as city in some books); the city itself, distinct from the hill/mountain of Zion as a place of Yahweh's dwelling.

stages.label: Jerusalem

quotes.quote: they buried him in David's city
a breach was made in the city

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs crowd the slopes; a fortified citadel of the stronghold of Zion stands on the high ground. Massive city walls with gates, and above the city the temple mount crowned by a stone-built temple of Yahweh.

fields.primarySubject: Jeremiah standing upright, cloaked, one hand raised toward the east
fields.action: He receives and turns toward the distant east as the word of Yahweh is given to him.
fields.setting: The walls and gate of Jerusalem overlooking open desert and distant eastern hills.
fields.secondaryElements: A faint radiance or cloud of light gathering above the eastern horizon as a sign of Yahweh's word, few onlookers on the walls.
fields.mood: Solemn, weighty and attentive, with quiet grief and dignity.
fields.timeOfDay: Late afternoon, warm low sun, hot desert haze over distant lands.
fields.composition: Wide view from the city wall, Jeremiah in the foreground left, the eastern horizon stretching across the right.

moment.text: Eber lived four hundred thirty years after he became the father of Peleg, and became the father of more sons and daughters.

fields.primarySubject: Elderly Eber seated at the tent entrance, relaxed and content
fields.action: A family gathering at dusk, children and servants settling around the evening meal
fields.setting: Scattered tents and a herding camp on the edge of a mud-brick town
fields.secondaryElements: Several sons and daughters of varying ages, a woman tending a cooking pot, herding staffs leaning against the tent, water skins hanging nearby
fields.mood: Quiet continuity, dignity and fullness of life
fields.timeOfDay: Late day, clear dry sky with warm low sunlight and long soft shadows

aliases: the God of our Lord Jesus Christ
him who sits on the throne
canon.name: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel
canon.note: The one God, creator and speaker of the Old Testament and the Father of Jesus Christ in the New Testament; distinct from Jesus in every entry.

stages.label: God the Father (radiance and cloud)

quotes.quote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.

stages.text: God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

canon.name: Moses
canon.note: Israel's lawgiver and leader who led the people out of Egypt, received the law at Sinai and is named across the Old and New Testament divisions as the same individual, distinguished only by the sections in which he appears or is mentioned.

stages.label: Moses, elder

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

stages.text: Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.

stages.label: Moses, infant

quotes.quote: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

stages.text: Moses: a newborn infant; soft smooth skin; a small round face; a little dark hair; wrapped in plain linen cloth and laid in a woven reed basket sealed with bitumen and pitch; no beard, no staff, no adult clothing.

stages.label: Moses, adult

quotes.quote: But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

stages.text: Moses: a man of about forty; lean, strong, well-proportioned build; brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard; alert, sober face; a knee-length undyed linen tunic with a dark woven wool cloak of brown and grey pinned at the shoulder; he carries a plain wooden shepherd's staff.

canon.name: Aaron, brother of Moses
canon.note: Moses' older brother and first high priest, in Exodus and in Numbers (census, offerings, death on Mount Hor); the same man across both divisions.

stages.label: Aaron, the first high priest

quotes.quote: Amram took Jochebed his father’s sister to himself as wife; and she bore him Aaron and Moses.
Of the blue, purple, and scarlet, they made finely worked garments for ministering in the holy place, and made the holy garments for Aaron
Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.

stages.text: Aaron: man in his eighties, older brother of Moses; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and close-cropped hair; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a blue robe, a woven ephod of blue, purple and scarlet, a breastplate, and a linen headband. Props: none carried alone; the rod of the Exodus is sometimes held.

aliases: the tent of meeting outside the camp
canon.name: the camp of Israel
canon.note: The Israelite encampment in the wilderness, with the tent of meeting set outside it in Exodus 33; the same encampment that Leviticus calls the camp.

stages.label: the camp of Israel

quotes.quote: the pillar of cloud moved from before them, and stood behind them.
quail came up and covered the camp; and in the morning the dew lay around the camp.
Moses used to take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, far away from the camp
outside of the camp to a clean place where the ashes are poured out

stages.text: the camp of Israel: a wide wilderness encampment of dun-coloured tents of woven goat-hair cloth in ordered rows, with a central sanctuary tent and a gate; bare stony desert plain, scattered acacia and tamarisk, distant dark mountain slopes; a pillar of cloud above the camp by day and fire by night; ash-pits and a clean place beyond its edges.

aliases: the door of the Tent of Meeting
the court of the Tent of Meeting
canon.name: the tabernacle (portable sanctuary)
canon.note: The one portable sanctuary of the wilderness, described in Exodus 25-40 and referred to as the Tent of Meeting in Leviticus and Numbers; all three entries are the same place.

stages.label: The tabernacle (portable sanctuary)

quotes.quote: made the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twined linen, blue, purple, and scarlet. They made them with cherubim
He made curtains of goats’ hair for a covering over the tabernacle.
He made the boards for the tabernacle, twenty boards for the south side southward.
the sockets around the court, the sockets of the gate of the court, all the pins of the tabernacle

stages.text: The tabernacle: a portable sanctuary of a rectangular tent of fine twined linen curtains in blue, purple and scarlet woven with cherubim, over a covering of goats' hair and rams' skins, stretched over upright acacia boards overlaid with gold, set in silver sockets and held by gold-covered bars, enclosed by a court of white linen hangings on bronze pillars.

fields.primarySubject: A solitary woman in a plain woven tunic and cloak, standing with her head lowered and hands folded.
fields.action: She stands apart in quiet isolation, her companions holding back in respectful distance.
fields.setting: The edge of the Israelite camp, goat-hair tents at a distance, sand and rocky ground beyond.
fields.secondaryElements: A couple of women standing a short way off, a priest in linen garments walking past at the edge of the frame, the tabernacle's distant outline.
fields.mood: Quiet, sorrowful and dignified, with a sense of solemn separation.
fields.timeOfDay: Daytime, dry desert air, steady clear light.
fields.composition: Medium shot from a low angle, the woman placed slightly off-center with open ground and tents receding behind her.

aliases: Abraham the father of many nations
canon.name: Abram
canon.note: Son of Terah from Ur, called to Canaan and renamed Abraham; the same patriarch as Galatians' Abraham, so both entries form one cluster.

stages.label: Abram / Abraham

quotes.quote: Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.
Abraham was one hundred years old when his son, Isaac, was born to him.
Abraham gave up his spirit, and died at a good old age, an old man, and full of years
Lot went with him.

stages.text: Abram, later Abraham: an elderly man of seventy-five to one hundred years and beyond; lean, weathered build from years of travel; dark skin tanned by desert sun; short greying beard and hair; deep-set, steady eyes and lined face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed wool wrap over a earth-brown linen tunic, leather sandals. Signature prop: a long wooden herder's staff.

canon.name: Cave of Machpelah
canon.note: Burial cave Abraham bought from Ephron the Hittite, resting place of the patriarchs and their wives; distinct from the other fields.

stages.label: Cave of Machpelah

quotes.quote: the cave of Machpelah, which he has, which is in the end of his field
in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre (that is, Hebron), in the land of Canaan

stages.text: Cave of Machpelah: a natural limestone cave opening into a hillside at the far end of a walled field near Mamre, outside the town of Hebron. Rough grey rock with dry ochre streaks; a low, narrow mouth fronted by a flat threshold stone. Oak and terebinth trees stand near the field, with wild grasses and thorny scrub. Small dry-stone wall marks the field boundary; sparse olive trees on the slope.

fields.primarySubject: Abraham kneeling at the cave mouth, bearing the wrapped body of Sarah
fields.action: Laying the dead wife into the tomb in the rock
fields.setting: Hillside field before Mamre with terebinth trees and a rock-hewn cave
fields.secondaryElements: Dry grass, a few stone markers, the cave entrance hewn into the limestone
fields.mood: Solemn grief and quiet dignity
fields.timeOfDay: Late afternoon, clear and still, warm amber sun low over the western hills
fields.composition: Medium-wide view from the field, Abraham centred at the cave mouth with the trees framing the hill
